title: Hosted→Edge Consumption Transition Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary

This playbook describes the product, operational, and commercial steps required to transition customers from Redwood Hosted inference to an Edge-enabled consumption model (on-prem / regional edge nodes / partner-hosted edge). The goal is to enable lower egress latency, localized data residency, and reduced long-tail token costs for high-volume interactive workloads while preserving SLA guarantees and unit economics.

Audience
- Product managers and engineering leads responsible for the Hosted→Edge journey
- Solutions and customer success teams running onboarding
- Platform and runtime engineers implementing edge delivery features
- Pricing and finance owners validating commercial flows

Objectives
1. Define a repeatable onboarding path for Hosted customers that want to run inference on regional/partner edge nodes.
2. Align SLO mappings and crediting so customers have predictable costs and latency targets post-transition.
3. Provide a minimal viable observability and rollback plan to keep availability and fidelity guarantees intact.

Scope and out-of-scope
- In scope: model routing policies, consumption metering changes, packaging/pricing blueprints, telemetry and guardrails, a canonical rollout sequence (pilot → phased → GA).
- Out of scope: custom edge hardware procurement, on-prem hardware installation SOPs (covered by eng-private-deployments), and partner commercial negotiations.

Key success metrics (KPI)
- Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end request latency reduced by >= 40% for pilot tenants relative to Hosted baseline.
- Cost: per-token billable cost change within +/- 10% of modeled estimate after first-month usage.
- Adoption: 10 pilot customers onboarded within Q3 pilot window.
- Reliability: No more than one customer-facing incident attributable to transition per 1000 hours of tenant traffic during pilot.

Stakeholders and ownership
- Product owner: Aisha Patel (product) — overall playbook shepherd
- Runtime engineering: Daniel Kim (eng-serving-runtime) — routing, KV/cache coordination, model pinning
- Edge infra & packaging: Sofia Martinez (eng-private-deployments) — packaging and day-2 ops checklist
- Customer success: Priya Rao (customer-success) — onboarding & QBRs
- Pricing & finance: Marco Alvarez (finance-legal) — consumption models and contract amendments

High-level approach
1. Pilot: 3-5 customers, single-edge-region capability, curated model variants (latency-optimized) and conservative SLOs.
2. Phased expansion: scale to multiple regions and partner nodes; introduce automated affinity and hybrid routing (edge fallback to hosted).
3. GA: standardized packaging, commercial SKU, console UX flows, and self-serve migration for small/mid customers.

Technical prerequisites and checklist
- Edge node runtime: runtime image with same inference-kernel compatibility as Hosted, accepts same model manifest format.
- Model artifact sync: secure artifact replication with checksum validation and version pinning.
- KV/prefix cache coordination: prefix cache invalidation and warm-start instructions.
- Telemetry contract: consistent telemetry tags (tenant_id, route_id, model_variant, region, host_type) and heartbeat metrics.
- Routing & fallback: policy layer that supports region-based affinity + automatic fallback to hosted variants on capacity or model-mismatch.

Required telemetry and reports
1. Migration readiness report (pre-cutover): model size/distribution, request mix (chat vs. single-turn), peak concurrency per-tenant.
2. Post-cutover validation: latency P50/P95, token-rate, cache hit ratio, model-consistency checksums, observed vs. forecasted spend.
3. Monthly economic reconciliation: billed tokens vs. estimated tokens (edge vs. hosted), variance explanation.

SLO and billing alignment (summary table)
- SLO Mapping (example):
  - Hosted primary SLO: 99.5% success within 300ms P95 for short prompts → Edge pilot SLO: 99.5% success within 200ms P95 (regional)
  - Cost guarantee: initial 30-day stabilization window where finance applies an 'onboarding adjustment' credit if variances exceed threshold.

Consumption & pricing implications
- Hybrid metering: token usage should be attributed to the serving location (edge-region or hosted fallback).
- Price buckets: define two SKU modifier bands: Edge-Latency (premium 5–15%) and Edge-Basic (no premium).
- Commitment & credits: enterprise pilots include a 3-month credit buffer to absorb variance; breakdown in contract appendix.

Migration sequence (detailed steps)
1. Preflight (2–4 weeks)
   - Collect migration readiness report and perform synthetic load tests against cached model artifacts.
   - Product and CS review: risk assessment and go/no-go checklist signed by customer.
2. Provisioning (1–3 days)
   - Deploy model artifacts to customer/partner edge region via secure sync.
   - Configure tenant routing policy and quota limits in control plane.
3. Canary (24–72 hours)
   - Route 1–5% traffic to Edge with canary telemetry tag. Monitor latency, error rate, and model-output regressions (use eval prompts).
   - Automatic rollback triggers: > 5% increase in P95 latency vs baseline OR output regression rate > threshold.
4. Ramp (1–4 weeks)
   - Increase traffic by doubling percentage every 48 hours while monitoring KPIs.
   - Apply consumption crediting until first invoice cycle reconciles usage.
5. Stabilize & GA handoff
   - Move to standard SKU pricing; update contract terms. Provide runbook and 30-day watch window.

Rollback and incident playbook
- Immediate rollback criteria:
  - P95 latency regression > 30% relative to Hosted baseline sustained for 10 minutes.
  - Token discrepancy > 15% vs logger estimates for two consecutive hourly windows.
- Rollback steps:
  1. Switch tenant routing to Hosted primary in control plane with sticky session drain (30–120s).
  2. Revoke edge model executions and collect diagnostics bundle (trace + logs + artifact checksums).
  3. Customer comms template: status, mitigation steps, ETA.

Developer & customer UX changes
- Console: new "Edge migration" workflow with readiness checks, canary controls, and cost preview.
- API: new field in route configuration: "edge_preference": [regional, latency, cost] and "edge_fallback_policy".
- SDK: sample snippet for toggling edge routing and verifying model checksum.

Operational runbook excerpts
- Preflight CLI commands (example):
  - redwood ctl migration preflight --tenant <TENANT> --region eu-west-edge --report out.json
  - redwood ctl model sync --tenant <TENANT> --model <MODEL_ID> --target-edge <EDGE_NODE>

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Model drift between hosted and edge artifacts → Mitigation: artifact checksum validation + nightly consistency checks and automated re-sync.
- Risk: Cost overruns due to inefficient batching on small edge nodes → Mitigation: conservative batching policy, telemetry-driven batching tuning, and credit buffer.
- Risk: Observability blind spots across partner nodes → Mitigation: federated telemetry ingestion contract and mandatory heartbeat metrics.

Appendix A — Example billing adjustment bands (illustrative)
- Variance <= 10%: no adjustment
- Variance 10–20%: 50% of variance credited for first cycle
- Variance > 20%: full review and potential extended credit up to 90% while root cause investigated

Appendix B — Minimal console checklist (to be shown in product UI)
1. Confirm model compatibility: architecture, tokenizer, quantization profile
2. Verify artifact checksum and size
3. Run synthetic latency test < 3x Hosted P95 threshold
4. Accept onboarding credit terms and SLA mapping
5. Start canary and monitor for 72 hours

- Pilot launch (Q4 2028): recruit 3 pilot customers and run the first migrations.
